Reason: Visual inspection confirms a larger right-sided pleural effusion (blunting of the right costophrenic angle) compared to the left, and multiple bilateral nodular opacities are visible; among the choices, septic emboli best explains the combination of cavitating/nodular lesions with effusion, whereas Wegener's typically presents with upper-lobe predominance and PE does not cause nodules. *(guided by t000003)*
